 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of July 21, 2020.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of July 21, 2020.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  This is the presentation of the “Register of Demands and Warrants” for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 4, 2020  2
   C. PHOENIX GROUP INFORMATION SYSTEMS CITATION PROCESSING
  SYSTEM CONTRACT

  The contract for the Police Department’s current citation processing system,
  Phoenix Group Information Systems, expired in September 2019. Other
  competitive vendors have provided presentations for services; however, have
  not been qualified to meet the City’s parking citation processing needs. Staff
  has conducted a comparative analysis with other competitive vendors to
  determine the best qualified vendor for citation processing.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the City Manager to execute
  a five-year contract with Phoenix Group Information Systems for parking-
  citation processing and online overnight-permit processing and management
  services.

  D. AGREEMENT FOR USE OF SMITH PARK POOL BY SAN GABRIEL SEA
  GULLS

  On June 30, 2020, the Agreement between the City of San Gabriel and the
  San Gabriel Sea Gulls for the use of Smith Park Pool expired. The San Gabriel
  Sea Gulls (SGSG) use Smith Park Pool for its swim team practices and swim
  meets. Typically, the team uses the pool during the school year and summer
  months. Due to COVID-19, the pool has been closed since March of this year.
  With the reopening of Smith Park Pool in accordance with Los Angeles County
  Health Order, the SGSG anticipate restarting its program and using Smith Park
  Pool by late August.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council approve the attached agreement
  between the City of San Gabriel and San Gabriel Sea Gulls for the use of Smith
  Park Pool, effective immediately and ending on June 30, 2021, with the option
  to renew automatically for two additional one-year terms.

  E. AGREEMENT FOR USE OF SMITH PARK POOL BY MONTEREY PARK
  MANTA RAYS

  The Monterey Park Manta Rays (MPMR) approached the City in June about
  using the Smith Park Pool for their regular swim team practices. The
  agreement allows MPMR use of the pool during mutually agreed upon dates

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 4, 2020  3
   and times and requires that they adhere to all emergency public health
  protocols established by the Los Angeles County Department of Public
  Health.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the attached agreement
  between the City of San Gabriel and the Monterey Park Manta Rays for the
  use of Smith Park Pool, effective immediately and ending on June 30, 2021.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. IMPACTS OF ELIMINATING OR REDUCING FEES TO APPEAL A VARIANCE
  DECISION

  At the June 16, 2020 Council meeting, City Council requested that an item be
  agendized to have a discussion of the possible impacts from reducing or
  eliminating fees to appeal a variance decision made by the Planning
  Commission. This report will analyze the pros and cons of such actions.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss and provide direction to staff
  on whether or not they want to reduce or eliminate variance appeal fees.

  B. CONSIDERATION FOR CITY OF SAN GABRIEL TO JOIN A LAWSUIT AS A
  PLAINTIFF SEEKING TO BLOCK AN ATTEMPT BY THE TRUMP
  ADMINISTRATION TO EXCLUDE PERSONS BASED ON CITIZENSHIP AND
  IMMIGRATION STATUS FROM THE 2020 CENSUS COUNT
  APPORTIONMENT BASE

  The City Council will consider whether to join a lawsuit with City of San Gabriel
  as a plaintiff to stop defendants from excluding persons from population
  counts and apportionment determinations following the 2020 Census on the
  basis of citizenship and immigration status that would in effect deprive cities
  with relatively high numbers of immigrants, such as San Gabriel, of equal
  representation in Congress and threaten the City’s ability to obtain resources
  needed to deliver vital City services.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 4, 2020  4
   It is recommended that the Council consider joining the lawsuit by Common
  Cause et. al. as a plaintiff to prevent harm to the City and its residents that
  would result from excluding persons from the 2020 Census enumeration and
  apportionment determinations based on citizenship and immigration status.

  7. PUBLIC COMMENT

  8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  11. ADJOURNMENT

  The next Regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, August 18, 2020
  at 6:30 p.m. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will
  be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website
  at www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF AUGUST 4, 2020
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

CALL TO ORDER

Mayor Menchaca called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
6:33 P.M. on Tuesday, August 4, 2020, with all Council Members and staff participating by
teleconference.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Menchaca.

ROLL CALL

Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Jason Pu, Vice Mayor
  Chin Ho Liao, and Mayor Denise Menchaca.
Council Members Absent:  None.
Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux,  Assistant  City  Manager/Community
  Development Director Arminé Chaparyan, Community
  Services/Interim Mission Playhouse Director Rebecca
  Perez, Police Chief Eugene Harris, Chief City Clerk
  Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg
  de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Interim Finance Director Kenneth Louie, and Assistant
  City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas.

City Manager Lazzaretto announced that the format for Council input on each item would
be altered from asking each Council Member individually for a response, to a general
request for input from Council Members, in order to increase meeting efficiency.
1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objections, Mayor Menchaca announced that the agenda order was
  approved.

2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. RECOGNITION OF NATIONAL NIGHT OUT

  The presentation was made by Police Chief Harris.

  B. COVID-19 BRIEFING

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 5  August 4, 2020
   Mayor Menchaca announced that this will be an ongoing presentation on the
  Agenda until the COVID-19 pandemic ends to keep the public informed directly
  from the City’s first responders and staff.

  Presentations were made by Fire Chief Wallace; Police Chief Harris; and Assistant
  City Manager/Community Development Director Chaparyan, Vice Mayor Liao, and
  Council Member Ding reporting for the 10-Point Plan for Recovery, Resiliency and
  Reinvestment Subcommittee.

3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Doug Richter provided comments requesting that recommended speed limits, as
  presented in the Engineering and Traffic Survey in April 2020, be approved.

  Carina River, resident, provided comments expressing dissatisfaction with the City’s
  parking enforcement regulations and customer service related to parking permits.

  City Manager Lazzaretto explained that the speed survey item has been scheduled for
  the September 15, 2020, meeting as staff tries to schedule items so that meetings are
  not overly late; and that overnight parking enforcement has not resumed and the
  public will have plenty of notice before it resumes.

4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, seconded by Council Member Pu, to approve
  Consent Calendar Items 4A – 4E as presented.

  Motion approved Consent Calendar Items 4A – 4E as presented by a vote of 5-0 as
  follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the following items as presented:

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of July 21, 2020.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of July 21, 2020.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved the July 10, 2020, and July 17, 2020, Registers of
  Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  C. PHOENIX GROUP INFORMATION SYSTEMS CITATION PROCESSING SYSTEM
  CONTRACT

  The City Council approved the City Manager to execute a five-year contract with
  Phoenix Group Information Systems for parking-citation and online overnight-
  permit processing and management services.

  D. AGREEMENT FOR USE OF SMITH PARK POOL BY SAN GABRIEL SEA GULLS

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 5  August 4, 2020
   The City Council approved the agreement between the City of San Gabriel and San
  Gabriel Sea Gulls for the use of Smith Park Pool, effective immediately and ending
  on June 30, 2021, with the option to renew automatically for two additional one-
  year terms.

  E. AGREEMENT FOR USE OF SMITH PARK POOL BY MONTEREY PARK MANTA
  RAYS

  The City Council approved the agreement between the City of San Gabriel and the
  Monterey Park Manta Rays for the use of Smith Park Pool, effective immediately
  and ending on June 30, 2021.

5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. IMPACTS OF ELIMINATING OR REDUCING FEES TO APPEAL A VARIANCE
  DECISION
  The staff presentation was made by Management Specialist Mark Gallatin.

  City Manager Lazzaretto clarified that the City Council could give direction to
  change just the variance appeal fee in the Fee Schedule or the fees for all appeals;
  and recommended that the City Council not lower the appeal fee below the actual
  expenses to the City, with the possible exception of the staff costs.

  Chuck Sances provided comments suggesting that newspaper notices be
  eliminated in order to lower fees and that a letter signed by 24 residents be
  required for appeals.

  Discussion included: hard costs should be paid by the appellant and the appeal fee
  should be waived; removing an individual Council Member’s ability to waive the
  fee in favor of allowing a Council Member to request agendizing the item, with the
  vote of at least three Council Members at a future meeting to waive the fee;
  preference for fees not to be reduced and to retain the ability of one Council
  Member to waive the fee; variance requests have already been vetted by the
  Planning Commission; cost-breakdown for the appeal fee; fees for various Planning
  services; preference to keep fees the same now due to COVID-19 impacts, with a
  possible future increase to cover the cost to the City; a process already in place for
  review by the Planning and Design Review Commissions; and concern about
  frivolous appeals if the cost is lowered.

  There was a majority of the City Council in favor of making no changes to the
  variance appeal fees at this time.

  B. CONSIDERATION FOR CITY OF SAN GABRIEL TO JOIN A LAWSUIT AS A
  PLAINTIFF SEEKING TO BLOCK AN ATTEMPT BY THE TRUMP
  ADMINISTRATION TO EXCLUDE PERSONS BASED ON CITIZENSHIP AND
  IMMIGRATION STATUS FROM THE 2020 CENSUS COUNT APPORTIONMENT
  BASE

  The presentation was made by City Attorney Keith Lemieux.

  The following provided comments in opposition to the City joining the lawsuit:
  Robert Blundell; Linda Parmenter; and Alice Wong, resident.

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 5  August 4, 2020
   The following provided comments in favor of the City joining the lawsuit: Austin
  Raymundo; and Sean McMorris, resident.

  Dr. Chasity Jennings-Nuñez provided comments in favor of the City challenging
  any attempt to limit the voting strength, representation, or personhood of its
  residents.
  Isela Bowles provided comments recommending that Council Member Pu recuse
  himself from this item.

  City Attorney Lemieux clarified that Council Member Pu does not have a financial
  interest in this matter due to Common Cause providing the work on this case pro
  bono; and that there is the potential for some legal costs due to the possibility of
  related work by staff or the City Attorney’s office.

  Discussion included concern about potential lawsuits against the City and
  associated costs; negative impacts to the City and residents if all residents are not
  counted in the Census; potential legal costs; cost risk of participating in the lawsuit
  versus the impact a loss of funding would have; multiple other similar lawsuits;
  what kinds of legal costs might be incurred by the City; whether San Gabriel joins
  the case or not will not be determinative; fiduciary duty to the residents; risk of
  reprisal by the Trump Administration; concern about exposure to lawsuits due to
  perceived conflict of interest; other cities across the country will be considering
  joining the lawsuit; the City will benefit the same if the lawsuit prevails whether or
  not it is a party to the action; the option of adopting a resolution of support for
  the lawsuit; and joining the lawsuit with a cap of $5000 on expenditure without
  further City Council approval.

  There was a consensus of the City Council to direct staff to prepare a resolution of
  support for the lawsuit for consideration at the next City Council meeting.

7. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Debbie Kilgore provided comments expressing disapproval of the height of a
  condominium project at 235 S. Arroyo Drive.

8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto thanked the City Council, Executive Team, staff and the
  community for their support during the Coronavirus crisis. He clarified that the City’s
  eviction moratorium has expired, but our residents and businesses are still protected
  by the County’s moratorium, which has been extended through the end of September
  2020. In closing, he explained that the HEALS Act, which would replace the CARES Act,
  is going through the federal legislative process, and encouraged everyone who
  believes that local jurisdictions need federal support to reach out to their Senate and
  House representatives to urge them to support it.

9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Vice Mayor Liao reported on a press conference held by several cities at the County’s
  Supervisor’s office to demand fair allocation of the CARES Act funding; and provided
  an update that the rate increase proposed by Southern California Edison has been
  postponed to next year.

  Council Member Pu thanked his colleagues, the City Attorney’s office, and staff for the
  thoughtful consideration of New Business Item 6B. He reported that he and Mayor
  Menchaca, as members of the Subcommittee on Equity and Equality Issues, have
  continued meetings with community members and the business community; that they
CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 5  August 4, 2020
   will be having the first interfaith meeting with various faith institutions of the
  community; and will give a status report at the August 18, 2020, City Council meeting.

  Council Member Ding thanked the staff and Mayor Menchaca for good meeting
  efficiency; thanked Community Services/Interim Mission Playhouse Director Perez and
  staff for their work with the senior meal program; and announced a senior meal
  distribution provided by the Chiao Tung University Alumni Association of Southern
  California with food from Ding’s Garden Restaurant at the Mission Playhouse at 10:30
  A.M. on August 5, 2020.

  Council Member Harrington thanked staff for the meeting reports; thanked everyone
  for the lively discussion; and reminded the community to stay safe.

  Mayor Menchaca, with the assistance of Council Member Pu’s family members,
  virtually presented him with a ceremonial gavel and plaque commemorating his term
  as the 2019-2020 Mayor.

  Council Member Pu thanked Mayor Menchaca for the recognition as Outgoing Mayor.

10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

11. ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Menchaca adjourned the meeting at 9:08 P.M.

Respectfully submitted:

_____________________________________
JULIE NGUYEN, City Clerk

Approved this 18th day of August, 2020:

_____________________________________
DENISE MENCHACA, Mayor
